memory_candidates.content: When slimming a command/skill file by relocating and deleting a large block, per-section byte-budget estimates made before the retained content is actually composed can be badly wrong for the section that absorbs the retained functional core. In this task, the plan projected the retained 'STAGE 0' section at ~1,800 B based on the assumption that a deleted 'MULTI-TASK DISPATCH' block's replacement would net to near-zero; in practice the replacement had to keep real functional content (a validation loop, a dependency-graph build, a guard, and a full-key-set tool invocation plus its JSON delegation block) and landed at ~7,600 B -- 4x the estimate, and the single largest driver of a 2.3x budget overage. Lesson: when a plan requires specific functional content to survive intact (a stop-list of preserved semantics), treat the plan's own per-section byte estimates as provisional until the actual replacement text is drafted, and measure early rather than assuming the estimate will hold.

When deleting a code block that another script's test suite grep-asserts against (verifying the block's logic 'still exists' in a specific file), the deletion silently breaks that test even though the underlying behavioral contract has genuinely moved elsewhere and is still correct. The fix is not to delete the test case but to retarget its assertions at the NEW structural guarantee that makes the old check unnecessary (e.g., 'the file is always freshly initialized every invocation, so a foreign-session read is now structurally impossible' rather than 'grep for the comparison logic that used to guard against it'). Discovered via run-all.sh failing after deleting commands/orchestrate.md's MULTI-TASK DISPATCH Step 5, which test-session-runtime-files.sh's Case 2 grep-asserted against.
